resume_text: PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY Electrical Engineering student focused on ASIC/SoC design, FPGA development, and digital hardware verification. Experienced in RTL design, formal verification, synthesis, timing analysis, and hardware validation using SystemVerilog. Developing AI-driven FPGA accelerators and neural signal processing hardware, with a strong interest in high-performance, power-efficient silicon design. EDUCATION University of California, Santa Cruz - BS Electrical Engineering September 2026 - June 2028 In Progress Coursework: Signals & Systems, Computer Systems & Assembly Language Planned: Introduction to VLSI Digital System Design, High-Speed Digital Design, Logic Design, Computer Architecture Las Positas College, Livermore, CA - AS Electrical Engineering August 2023 - May 2026 Certifications: Electronics Foundations: Semiconductor Devices(LinkedIn), University of Colorado, Boulder: Hardware Description Languages for FPGA Design(Coursera), Arm: Computer Architecture Essentials(In Progress - Coursera) PROJECTS NeuroSig | Ongoing Personal Project | Github - Neural Signal Processing ASIC & Edge AI ● Designed and verified a 32-channel SystemVerilog neural signal-processing pipeline featuring fixed-point IIR filters, spike detection, and event merging, achieving 100% detection recall with zero false positives on a seeded 1M-sample synthetic test. ● Developed three spatial localization algorithms, including beamforming-inspired estimation and template matching, achieving 42.4 µm median localization error across noisy synthetic recordings. ● Built a hybrid ASIC-to-edge AI architecture with packetized neural data streaming and machine-learning inference, achieving 90.4% visual-stimulus classification accuracy on held-out Neuropixels recordings. Malleable AI FPGA | Ongoing Personal Project | Github - Designing an FPGA system to automatically optimize and adapt its resources to different AI models and footprints ● Designed a Verilog accelerator and memory-system RTL integrating HBM routing, asynchronous clock-domain crossings, arbitration, buffering, and host interfaces for configurable AI workloads. ● Developed configurable INT8/INT32 compute and datapath architecture with tiled accumulation, ReLU, requantization, and ping-pong buffering across multiple accelerator configurations. ● Reduced an HBM bridge datapath from 6,310 to 586 LUTs (~91%) by restructuring variable-selection logic, improving synthesized resource efficiency while preserving functionality. Jane Street Protocol Emulator ASIC Challenge | Ongoing | Github - Developing a cycle-accurate protocol-emulator ASIC targeting IHP 130 nm tapeout. ● Architected and implemented a custom 16-instruction RTL processor controlling 8 bidirectional I/O pins, executing UART, SPI, and I²C protocols as loadable firmware ● Designed processor control/datapath logic and integrated a programmable INT8 hardware classifier using time-multiplexed arithmetic for resource-efficient event classification. EEG Brain Signal Controlled Rover | WeaveHacks 4(Hackathon) - Collaborated in a 4-person team to leverage a multi-agent LLM system, which utilizes edge inference to control a hand-built rover through EEG brain waves. ● Architected an EEG-to-rover pipeline translating Bluetooth brain-signal data into real-time motor commands using custom transistor motor-control circuits. ● Built a multi-agent AI pipeline that normalized EEG signals against user baselines, improving command-reading accuracy by >50%. SKILLS Electronic Microcontrollers/FPGAs: Altera Quartus Cyclone V, AMD Virtex UltraScale+ HBM VU47P, Arduino, ESP32 Software Tools: Altera Quartus, Xilinx Vivado, ModelSim, LTSpice, KiCAD, Fusion360, Solidworks, LaTeX AI Platforms/Tools: Cursor, Codex Programming/Protocols: SystemVerilog , SVA, Verilog, VHDL, Python, C++, MATLAB, I²C, UART, PWM, SPI Equipment: Power Supply, Oscilloscope, Digital Multimeter, Soldering, Breadboard Prototyping EXPERIENCE Lead Math Tutor, Mathnasium - Livermore, CA August 2024 – March 2026 ● Explained algebra, geometry, and calculus while managing multiple learning plans and coordinating with instructors.
interests: ASIC, FPGA, digital verification, embedded systems, and software tools
